messages:
maya: Heads-up: deploying the new KV-prefix warmup rollout tomorrow 03:00 UTC. This is the final step of the caching work — it will seed popular key prefixes on cold nodes to reduce p99 token latency during traffic shifts. Expected user impact: small transient p99 blips, no errors. /cc @oncall @eng-sre :eyes:

alex: Thanks Maya. Can you post the SLO window and any temporary SLO relaxations so teams know what to expect?

maya: TL;DR: 03:00-05:00 UTC. We will temporarily relax the latency SLO for non-SLA tenants from 99.9% to 99.5% for token-gen p99 while warmup runs. SLA customers are not impacted (we’ll route them to reserved pools). Full details below.

maya: Plan overview:
- Start 03:00 UTC: roll warmup runtime to 10% of nodes (canary)
- 03:20: increase to 50% if canary metrics stable
- 04:00: 100% roll complete, run an additional 30m verification window
- 05:00: toggle policy back to normal

maya: What warmup does: it pre-populates KV prefixes K for recent request traces so new requests hit warmed ranges instead of incurring cold kv+model recompute. This reduces long-tail stalls but causes a short burst of behind-the-scenes IO during seeding.

maya: SRE Action items:
- Monitor p99 token latency (dash: https://dash.redwood.local/d/p99/kv-warmup) and kv-read ops (https://dash.redwood.local/d/kv-ops).
- We will lower alert thresholds for a temporary window: p99-alert -> 99.5. Alerts will auto-escalate if error rate > 0.5% for 10m.
- If you see sustained 5xxs or >1% error rate: abort rollout and engage oncall.

jon: Will this change autoscaler behavior? Any risk of spiking node CPU or OOMs?

maya: Autoscaler unchanged. Warmup uses low-priority background batches capped at 250 concurrent streams per node. We did perf testing — CPU p95 +8%, memory <2% increase. Still, please watch node-level CPU and OOMs.

sam: Product teams: if you have latency-sensitive routes, please add an explicit routing tag to pin them to dedicated pools during the window. Reach out if you need help.

lena: Is there a manual stop if things look bad?

maya: Yes. Two quick kill paths:
1) Kill warmup rollout via admin CLI: 
```
redwood-admin rollout cancel --component kv-warmup --env prod
```
2) Disable prewarm job scheduler: 
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment kv-warmup-scheduler --replicas=0
```
Either action will be executed by oncall if thresholds breach.

sre-oncall-bot: [AUTO] Alert policy adjusted for warmup window: p99-token-latency threshold lowered to 99.5% between 1976543210 and 1976543305.

alex: Noted. I'll coordinate with dedicated-pools team to ensure SLA traffic is pinned. Also posting a small notice to #customer-impact in case CSMs ask.

maya: Thanks. Post-roll verification checklist (we'll run at 04:30):
- p99 back to baseline within 15 minutes after end window
- error rate < 0.2%
- KV read ops within expected range
- No sustained node CPU > 85%

jon: Will you run a light load test during canary or just passive observation?

maya: Passive observation during canary. At 04:15 we'll run a short synthetic ramp (2m spike @ 20qps) to validate cold-path rate is reduced. Notifying load-test channel now.

sam: Anything for SREs on pager rotations?

maya: Oncall will own the safe-stop and escalation. If you're free during the window, please keep an eye on the dashboard. I'll be online for the whole rollout.

alex: Thanks everyone — sounds good. Logging this thread as the canonical announcement. :white_check_mark:
